summary: For every decision record standing PROPOSED, which owner-held category it actually touches, and whether STATUS.yaml already records the answer. decisions/0033 Ruling 1 says a question is settled at the lowest tier that can produce evidence defeating the alternatives, and decisions/0023 says only owner-held product intent, public naming, external commitment, irreversible external-world effect, and the acceptance standing itself reach Bdo. Every entry here is a claim with a reason, defeasible by him and by anyone else.
reading: reaches_owner false does not settle the record. It says the record can be settled below the owner and names why. Someone at that tier still has to do it.
already_recorded_note: already_recorded_as names a field or claim in STATUS.yaml that records the owner's answer to this record's question. Where one is present, the record's own status line is behind STATUS.yaml rather than genuinely open, and closing it is an edit rather than a judgement. The checker proves the named key is really in STATUS.yaml so this cannot be asserted loosely.
entry_keys_note: The whole vocabulary of a routing entry. There is deliberately no field that could record a settlement, an acceptance, or a date one happened: this file says who settles a record, never that anyone did. Recording an acceptance is STATUS.yaml's job and Bdo's act.
contested_note: An entry someone has pushed back on, naming the evidence. A routing table that quietly rewrites itself when challenged is worth less than one that shows where it was pushed, so the doubt is recorded beside the claim rather than replacing it. The entry still reads as its author left it until whoever holds the tier rules.
unit_note: v1 routed records and lost questions. A record can carry several questions with different answers - decisions/0036 names three, one for Control and one for Bdo - and a per-record reaches_owner boolean cannot represent that. Routing questions is what lets this file and a commit-range sweep reconcile without either being wrong. Found by an independent witness of 06be56c, not by this file's author.
ratification_note: Bare ratification is not routed. Every PROPOSED record needs it by definition, so counting it as a question that reaches Bdo would mark all eighteen and say nothing. This file answers the narrower question: does this need a judgement from him OTHER than the ratification every proposal already needs.
enumeration_note: enumerated_from records where a question came from. `record-section` means the record declares its own owner questions under a heading and each bullet became a question. `headline` means the record does not enumerate, so its single stated question is routed and any further question it carries implicitly is not yet visible here. Today exactly one record of eighteen enumerates its own questions, which is why this field is honest rather than decorative.

0001-A.question: founding-boundary
0001-A.reason: The founding boundary is product intent by definition. STATUS.yaml already lists the contract among accepted_repository_claims, so what is outstanding is the record's own status line, not the judgement.
0001-A.action_if_confirmed: Update the status line to match the claim STATUS.yaml already carries.

0003-A.question: evidence-boundary
0003-A.reason: How evidence binds is a rule about what the system is. STATUS.yaml carries the settled source claim; the record still reads as pending.

0007-A.question: asset-service-boundary
0007-A.reason: A chartered service boundary says what the system contains. Already an accepted repository claim.

0008-A.question: classification-contract
0008-A.reason: The vocabulary every other document reads. STATUS.yaml reads OWNER_ACCEPTED_CANONICAL_VOCABULARY.

0009-A.question: phase-i-logical-spec
0009-A.reason: STATUS.yaml reads OWNER_ACCEPTED_PHASE_I_LOGICAL_SPEC_WITH_SOVEREIGNTY_CLARIFICATION. The record says OWNER FREEZE PENDING. Freeze and acceptance are different acts and only one of them happened, which is why this one also touches acceptance_standing.
0009-A.action_if_confirmed: Ask the narrower question: accepted is recorded, frozen is not. Does he want it frozen?

0010-A.question: proofing-service-boundary
0010-A.reason: STATUS.yaml reads RULED_SECOND_BOUNDARY_O11_CHARTERED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. The boundary stands as a reversible default under decisions/0046, which states that none of its rulings is an owner acceptance, so the acceptance itself is outstanding and not only the record's status line. An earlier duplicate of this field spelled it OWNER_ACCEPTED_BOUNDARY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED and was dead text a YAML reader never saw; this entry read that spelling before it was deleted.

0016-A.question: github-coordination-registrar
0016-A.reason: Already an accepted claim. It keeps external_commitment because the registrar reaches a service outside this machine whenever it is actually used.
0016-A.action_if_confirmed: Update the status line; the external crossing stays gated separately.

0018-A.question: verification-engagement-kind
0018-A.reason: A ticket kind is workflow vocabulary. It touches no owner-held category, and STATUS.yaml already carries the claim.
0018-A.action_if_confirmed: Close below the owner. Update the status line.

0019-A.question: kernel-transition-contract
0019-A.reason: Accepted, then moved: STATUS.yaml records the acceptance and, in a comment, that decisions/0034 changed the table afterwards. The open question is not the original acceptance but whether it survives the change.
0019-A.action_if_confirmed: Settle together with 0034; they are one question asked twice.

0020-A.question: owner-seat-topology
0020-A.reason: Genuinely open. No STATUS.yaml field or claim records an answer, and seat topology decides how authority is addressed, which is product intent. decisions/0035 and 0039 both now build on it.
0020-A.action_if_confirmed: Needs a real acceptance packet. Two later records depend on it.

0021-A.question: semantic-cold-start-task
0021-A.reason: An observation shape, already an accepted claim. No owner-held category.
0021-A.action_if_confirmed: Close below the owner. Update the status line.

0034-A.question: spec-transition-refusal-codes
0034-A.reason: Adds two refusal codes to a table Bdo already accepted, so the accepted table stops contradicting SPEC.md. It reaches him only because he accepted the earlier version.
0034-A.action_if_confirmed: One question, jointly with 0019. OPEN-SEAMS S17 is the same subject from the other end.

0035-A.question: seat-message-etiquette
0035-A.reason: Drafted at his direction, so the direction is settled and the wording is the question. It rules how every seat may speak, which is structural rather than an implementation choice.
0035-A.action_if_confirmed: Evidence exists: scripts/witness_seats.py, sixteen independent observations, plus fourteen defeating fixtures.

0036-A.question: Does this slice stand as the console's first, given the README named another?
0036-A.reason: Sequencing inside a boundary STATUS.yaml already records as owner-accepted, which decisions/0033 Ruling 1 assigns to Control. Evidence exists: scripts/witness_console.py, twenty independent observations.

0036-B.question: Should every Claude Code session in this repository open and close a console session automatically?
0036-B.reason: `.claude/settings.json` is checked in, so anyone who clones this repository and opens it in a Claude Code host writes an operator session to the journal at startup. That is a default applied to strangers, not a sequencing choice. v1 routed record 0036 on its first question alone and marked the whole record as not reaching him, dropping this one. Three independent readings say it reaches him: the record's own author, the QA sweep as its item 16, and the witness of 06be56c.
0036-B.action_if_confirmed: Ask it on its own. It is separable from the console slice and affects anyone who clones the repository.

0038-A.question: capability-map-front-and-back-office
0038-A.reason: contracts/capability-offices.json carries 79 authored assignments and every one sets required_authority - `asset.ingest-asset` to `ingest:asset` and so on. That file is an input to the build, not an output of it, so it is not the projection the v1 reason argued about. Assigning an authority type to every operation in the node is typed authority, which AGENTS.md reserves. The v1 entry argued against the door-inventory framing and never reached the authority assignment.
0038-A.action_if_confirmed: Ask about the authority assignment, not the map. The projection itself remains ordinary Control-tier work.
0038-A.contested_by: Witness of 06be56c: `reaches_owner: false` was wrong, on the required_authority ground rather than the door-inventory ground its author was arguing with. Independently, the QA sweep item 3 notes 0038 states as a constraint that no capability is served on MCP and that commit d850c6d served it. Both stand.

0039-A.question: the-node-surface
0039-A.reason: The largest genuinely open item. It promotes channel, thread and post to the node's primary interface for every actor, opens the federation boundary that SPEC.md and SYSTEM.md both defer, and rules the shape of a public surface. All three are product intent, and the public surface touches external commitment even at proposal standing.
0039-A.action_if_confirmed: Needs a real acceptance packet. This is the one worth his attention first.

0040-A.question: the-declared-service-surface
0040-A.reason: Makes each manifest operation an object carrying its preconditions and refusals instead of a bare string, so the conformance oracle can test a refusal it was never told to expect. A schema shape, defeasible by a fixture. No owner-held category.
0040-A.contested_by: Witness of 06be56c, flagged rather than dissented: 0040 declares per-operation refusal codes that previously existed only in Python, and CLASSIFICATION.md owns vocabulary. The witness was not confident either way and neither is this entry. Left at reaches_owner false with the doubt recorded.

0041-A.question: the-observation-service
0041-A.reason: A chartered service boundary says what the system contains, which is the shape 0007 and 0010 already route to the owner. STATUS.yaml carries the field and it reads CHARTERED_BOUNDARY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, so the acceptance itself is outstanding, not only the record's status line. This entry once drew that contrast against an OWNER_ACCEPTED_ wording on 0010's field; that wording was a duplicate a YAML reader never saw, 0010's field reads RULED_ under decisions/0046, and the two now stand alike. Drafted at Bdo's direction; direction is not acceptance.
0041-A.action_if_confirmed: Present the boundary for acceptance, then update both the status line and observation_service_status.

0042-A.question: the-decision-queue-is-not-a-queue
0042-A.reason: Proposes machinery over the acceptance rule itself, which decisions/0023 names as owner-held. It settles no decision and changes no status line, but it does decide how the queue in front of him is assembled, and that is his.
0042-A.action_if_confirmed: Accept or reject the routing shape. Rejecting it leaves the seventeen records exactly where they were.

0044-A.question: github-coordination-write-crossing
0044-A.reason: The read half is already accepted as github_coordination_registrar_and_typed_ticket_workflow. This adds a write half that mutates a public repository, which is an irreversible external effect and owner-held however carefully it is gated. Bdo directed the crossing type; he has not accepted this shape of it. The record is also contested on the facts: it states that no lawful write path existed, and decisions/0057-board-management-role.md on main had declared one nineteen hours earlier. Both define adapters/github/apply.py and neither is a superset.
0044-A.action_if_confirmed: Hold at the owner. Reconcile against decisions/0057-board-management-role.md before presenting, since accepting both would admit two write paths to one surface.
0044-A.contested_by: Open-PR review of 2026-08-24: main and feat/federation-harness-and-hardening each implement the whole coordination surface, written blind.

SWEEP-01.question: Is NONE an admissible effect class, and DERIVED, REBUILT, SUPERSEDE, REBUILD, counters?
SWEEP-01.reason: Six manifests use effect-class values CLASSIFICATION.md does not define. Either the owner-accepted vocabulary grows or six manifests are wrong, and CLASSIFICATION.md is vocabulary he accepted.
SWEEP-01.action_if_confirmed: Rule the vocabulary once; six manifests follow from it.

SWEEP-02.question: Does bindings/mcp/ need a decision record before it stays a required check?
SWEEP-02.reason: 820 lines that open sessions, issue grants, write to the operational record, and one endpoint spawns the repository gate itself. It is a required verify.py check and no decision record covers it.
SWEEP-02.action_if_confirmed: Either admit it with a record or drop it from the gate until one exists.

SWEEP-03.question: Is decisions/0038 admitted retroactively?
SWEEP-03.reason: 0038 states as a constraint that no capability is served on MCP and that standing up a stdio surface is not admitted by it. Commit d850c6d, the next commit, did exactly that.
SWEEP-03.action_if_confirmed: Amend 0038 or withdraw the surface. Overlaps 0038-A and is counted once.

SWEEP-04.question: Is caller-asserted attribution acceptable over a binding?
SWEEP-04.reason: The MCP gateway takes actor as a tool argument and the asset receipt records it unchecked, so one act leaves two records naming different actors. The console had the same shape with granted_by defaulting to the owner's own name.
SWEEP-04.action_if_confirmed: Rule whether identity may arrive as an argument at all, or must come from a check.

SWEEP-05.question: Which scope semantics is the node's?
SWEEP-05.reason: Console matches scope by exact string, so a grant scoped * admits only an operation scoped *. Asset treats * as a wildcard. One node, two meanings, and nothing reconciles them.
SWEEP-05.action_if_confirmed: Pick one and make the other conform.

SWEEP-06.question: Does a COUNTERED crossing admit its origin onto the public surface?
SWEEP-06.reason: federation.py treats COUNTERED as admitting, alongside COMMITTED. The crossing schema defines COUNTERED as contradicting the peer. With the only inbound crossing at COUNTERED the peer's thread publishes.
SWEEP-06.action_if_confirmed: A semantic call about what countering means at a node boundary.

SWEEP-07.question: Is public-projection.schema.json the target, or is the console's simpler view the real one?
SWEEP-07.reason: The console documents published_threads() as the read built over that schema; driven live it produces 12 defects and 10 of 13 required properties absent. Two descriptions of one surface and no test links them.
SWEEP-07.action_if_confirmed: Name which is authoritative; the other changes to match.

SWEEP-08.question: Which of the three readings of INCOMPLETE_PROPOSAL holds?
SWEEP-08.reason: Declared in six manifests and in the kernel table, emitted by nothing. OPEN-SEAMS S17 records the three readings and none is settled.
SWEEP-08.action_if_confirmed: Rule it; the seam closes either way.

SWEEP-09.question: Should a service manifest carry standing at all?
SWEEP-09.reason: A manifest may declare its own standing as WITNESSED or RATIFIED and the checker accepts it. A build cannot witness itself, so a self-declared standing is a claim no participant may make. All six are honest today.
SWEEP-09.action_if_confirmed: Constrain the field to PROPOSED|BUILT, or remove it.

SWEEP-10.question: Is outward publication a root-seat judgement or work any seat may perform?
SWEEP-10.reason: OPEN-SEAMS S19. The projection contract wants a seat, the console record carries an operator id, and nothing bridges them.
SWEEP-10.action_if_confirmed: Rule the relation; the two contracts reconcile from it.

SWEEP-11.question: Should opening this repository write an operator session automatically?
SWEEP-11.reason: Same question as 0036-B, reached independently by the sweep. Bdo answered No on 2026-08-24 and named a template file as the remedy.
SWEEP-11.action_if_confirmed: Answered. Carried as a duplicate so the two readings visibly reconcile.

SWEEP-12.question: Is a self-authored subprocess-only checker an independence claim?
SWEEP-12.reason: Several commits this session claim independence on the strength of not importing the code under test. Whether that is independence or only distance is a question about what witnessing means, which reaches the acceptance standing directly.
SWEEP-12.action_if_confirmed: Rule what independence requires; every witness report depends on the answer.

one_list_note: Bdo ruled on 2026-08-24 that he wants one merged list. A question therefore enters here whether it comes from a decision record or from somewhere else, and `source` says which. Two mechanisms may still exist - a gate that stops work being parked on him and this census of what is already written are different jobs with different failure modes - but only one of them publishes a number, and it is this one.
same_as_note: Two sources reaching the same question. The duplicate is kept rather than deleted so the agreement between two independent readings stays visible, and it is excluded from every count.
